svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D5 — Chapter 5 · Ch05_ThetaZSpaces, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,842 declarations of the 79 items on C5, each with its kind, file, line and state; 93 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,842 declarations of the 79 items on C5, each with its kind, file, line and state; 93 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C5's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

text.tspan: · p. 223 · 47 declarations, 12 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: A function on the regular locus admits a continuation with bounded poles if it extends in the complex coordinates with the prescribed lower bounds on order.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The coordinates are centered at each point. The continuation is required to be analytic at every point where the order bound permits no pole.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: These are the closure fields for the submodule of regular restrictions.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We represent the functions by their regular values and use the pole order bounds and compact convergence topology specified in §5.1.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This checks the target in the case where no poles are allowed.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The simple-pole bound from §5.1.3 is built into the target here.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The target uses the bounded-pole model of §5.1.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We use the nonpositive part of the meromorphic order, as in §3.3.1. The bound is zero at the zeros of the correcting factor.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This checks the order bound against the real Tate factor.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The target uses the bounded-pole model of §5.1.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We take the kernel on S-ideles. The descended theta map has the same kernel because the map from S-ideles to S-idele classes is surjective.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We read the two-argument L_T as the test-function transform Z_T of §5.1 and record (5.2.3.4) as an identity of transforms for arbitrary tests. The proof invokes it under source-kernel vanishing on p. 233 and target-kernel vanishing on p. 234. The missing mass affects the identity but cancels in both kernel arguments. Global extensions parametrize the indicated local

g.text: The introduction says that the local Fourier maps tend to “the inversion automorphism” on the global theta space.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We read inversion as pullback of theta functions by g ↦ g⁻¹ on idele classes. existsUnique_globalThetaFourier gives the Fourier automorphism, whose action on theta values is governed by adelicTheta_riemannRoch. See ERRATA F29.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Restrict theta-null tests to the face x_v = 0, giving the space of all traces the quotient topology from tests.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This is what remains of the criterion sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer, which is proved from it below. Proved in Lean, and excluded here by hypothesis: the case in which the classes span a finite-dimensional space (hS), and the case in which they are given by even real Schwartz profiles (hreal; it covers ℚ with no finite place). The other direction of the criterion is proved

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: in Lean as well (sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_general_forward). The hypotheses hk, hM and hm follow from the bounds and are proved before this statement is applied. The bounds are written without derivatives, which is equivalent (sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_zeroth_iff), and the conclusion is boundedness in the quotient, which is equivalent to

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: representatives in one bounded set (sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_lift_iff_quotient_bounded). The paper states its results for bornological spaces and in the variable of the idele classes. Writing them for this library is the project's work and is not proved in Lean: that the bounded sets of the Schwartz–Bruhat space here are the paper's, that the kernel of the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: S-unit sum is the closed span the paper divides by, the normalizations of the Fourier transform and of the Haar measures, and the seminorms on the dual group. The integrator and an independent reviewer checked these steps against the paper for the whole criterion (#7346); no specialist in the paper's framework has.

g.text: The single-place operator at v is 1 minus the normalized average over the integer units at v of the translates by the reciprocal uniformizer times the unit, and S-local theta turns this into the same recipe on the theta function: theta of the principal value at one place is theta of the test minus the normalized average, over the integer units at that place, of theta of its translates.

g.text: A function on the unit group has an additive Schwartz extension vanishing at zero exactly when it is locally constant and compactly supported there.

g.text: The finite punctured test space in (5.3.4.1) is interpreted as compactly supported locally constant tests, consistently with Remark 2.1.2.1.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The finite punctured factors in (5.3.4.1) are compactly supported tests on the units. The subspace has the topology inherited from the S-adelic Schwartz space of Proposition 2.1.4.1, which uses the inductive archimedean–finite tensor topology. The span identity below is algebraic. The projective topology in print is generally coarser.

g.text: We use the unitary-lift coordinates of Remark 5.4.1.2. The normalized lift for a chosen section recovers the coordinates of Theorem 5.4.1.1. If the lift has frequency x on the section, both entries, as functions of s here, shift by +ix. The unreflected Fourier Mellin transform separately has frequency -x.
